minutes.headline: Sewer Commission elected a new chair and clerk and approved two large Mass One pump station repairs.
minutes.summary: The commission reorganized with two new members: Mike Mackin was elected chair, Scott Doll clerk, and Brett Ramon was re-elected vice chair. Staff reported the sewer business manager post is vacant after a recent resignation. The commission approved two cost estimates for repairs at the Mass One pump station and heard an FY24 budget update and a manhole repair bid update.

budget_items.what_was_said: One article transfers the FY24 excess of revenues over spending into the capital reserve stabilization fund. The commission had already voted on it at the prior meeting.

budget_items.topic: CTE estimate for Mass One force main repair
budget_items.what_was_said: The estimate was described as about seventy thousand with pumper trucks added; the manager judged it reasonable and comparable to last year's repair.

The FY25 budget put a large sum into capital repairs, enough to cover the Mass One repairs and possible Dana Street pump station work.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission approved two repair estimates for the Mass One pump station, one for the force main and one for the suction line, each by a unanimous roll call.
The commission reorganized, electing Mike Mackin chair and Scott Doll clerk; Brett Ramon was re-elected vice chair. Each nominee abstained on his own vote.
Staff reported the sewer business manager post is vacant after a resignation, and hiring of the assistant business manager is deferred until a business manager is in place.
Staff said FY24 closed with revenues above spending, and the FY25 budget puts money into capital repairs that can cover the Mass One work.
Customers on the affected Mass One line will get paper notice of the repair as well as social media posts.

why_it_matters: Pump station repairs are paid from sewer capital money, so they bear on sewer rates and on how much reserve is left for later work, such as the possible Dana Street pump station job.
The sewer business manager post is vacant, and the commission's role in hiring is still undecided, so who runs billing and day-to-day finances is unsettled.
watch_next: Next meeting is October 8 at 6 PM by Zoom; the agenda is to include business manager updates, Mass One repair progress and grease trap permit renewal timing.
A special town meeting article would transfer the FY24 sewer surplus into the capital reserve stabilization fund; the commission already voted on it.
